Consult Summary:
- Nurse presenting with 7 days of fever and systemic symptoms after travel to Vietnam; plan to conduct in-person evaluation with targeted infectious workup including malaria testing.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Fever for about 7 days with hot/c sweaty episodes, generalized malaise, musculoskeletal aches, and nausea.
- Onset and course: Symptoms began ~7 days ago; fever persists with intermittent hot/cold periods; partial relief with OTC analgesics (ibuprofen and paracetamol) but not resolved.
- Associated symptoms: Fatigue; poor appetite; nocturnal sweating; muscle aches all over; headaches (related to screen use) but no focal neurological symptoms reported.
- Exposures/risks: Recently returned from Vietnam (4 weeks ago). Traveled actively in rural areas, trekking and cycling; exposure to countryside life. Took malaria prophylaxis (patient unclear of exact regimen; described as daily with another prophylactic on top). 
- Medical history: Chronic back pain; under physiotherapy for posture-related back issues.
- Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine) ongoing. OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol used daily.
- Allergies: Pollen allergy (hay fever).
- Vaccinations: Up to date (including Hepatitis B).
- Social history: Works as a nurse; non-smoker; moderate alcohol use; exercises moderately several times per week.
- Family history: Father had a heart attack in his sixties (age 68).
- Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No cough, sore throat, diarrhea, dysuria; no neck stiffness; no ear pain; no rashes; no joint swelling; head/eye symptoms not notable beyond routine headaches from screen exposure.
- Note on work: Unable to be at work until evaluation is completed.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain, managed with physiotherapy; posture-focused rehabilitation.
- No other chronic illnesses documented.
- Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine) listed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Pollen allergy (hay fever).

Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse.
- Smoking: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Moderate intake.
- Physical activity: Moderate exercise several times a week.
- Travel: Recent travel to Vietnam; 4 weeks since return; rural and urban exposure with trekking/cycling.

Family History:
- Father died of heart attack in his sixties (age ~68).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Examination findings: Not described in transcript.
- Notes: Examination planned in clinic; no documented exam findings from this encounter.

Investigations:
- Planned tests (mentioned by physician):
  - Thick and thin blood films to check for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers (general infectious/inflammatory workup).
  - Additional blood tests to follow based on exam findings.
- No imaging results or other test results documented in the transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1:
- Assessment: Fever with sweats, myalgias, nausea after recent travel to Vietnam; possible infectious etiology including malaria or other exotic infections pending workup.
- Plan:
  - Bring patient to in-person clinic in central London today for examination; alternative is local A&E if inconvenient.
  - Order blood tests including thick and thin malaria films and inflammatory markers; proceed with broader infectious workup as indicated after examination.
  - Document clinical reasoning in appointment notes to aid reception; admin to book appointment (patient instructed to call after a few minutes).
  - Advise that patient should not return to work until evaluation and testing are completed.
  - If central London visit is not feasible, patient can attend local A&E for urgent assessment.

Issue 2:
- Assessment: No focal infection identified yet; fever workup prioritized.
- Plan:
  - Continue with planned investigations first (malaria testing and inflammatory markers) and clinical assessment to guide further management.
  - No antibiotics or antiparasitic therapy initiated prior to results (not explicitly documented beyond the plan to test).

Issue 3:
- Assessment: Travel-related exposure risk and malaria prophylaxis details uncertain (patient unable to precisely recall prophylaxis regimen).
- Plan:
  - Verify and document malaria prophylaxis regimen during testing/clinic visit.
  - Consider malaria and other travel-related infections in differential diagnosis based on travel history and exposures.

General plan:
- Expedite in-person evaluation and malaria-focused testing; consider alternative pathways (central London clinic vs. local A&E) based on practicality.
- Communicate plan clearly to patient and arrange scheduling via administrative staff; patient instructed to contact number provided after a short interval.

Quality Checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals documented (not provided in transcript).
  - Physical examination findings (not described; exam planned).
  - Explicit allergies beyond pollen (documented) and full medication reconciliation (Seroxat listed; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Specific vaccination status beyond Hepatitis B (not further detailed; vaccination history noted as up to date).
- Internal conflicts:
  - Malaria prophylaxis details are uncertain from patient’s report, with conflicting impressions about daily vs. weekly regimens and “another one on top of the first.” This is noted as uncertainty but not a clear contradiction in the transcript.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; occasional minor misstatements due to conversation flow. No major inaudible sections; essential data captured for H&P.

Note: All information is transcribed exactly as stated; no additional clinical inferences or data have been added beyond the dialogue.
